newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba champions stability-driven monetary policy.
newsitem.headline: Buba champions stability-driven monetary policy.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Wednesday it must follow anti-inflationary policies to avoid distortions on financial markets and maintain its credibility.

The German central bank noted in its February monthly report that current historical lows in capital market interest rates had raised the risk of volatility on bond markets, as developments since the end of last year had shown.

"In this environment it is important not to allow any doubt to arise as to the firm stability orientation of monetary policy and as to the lasting consolidation of state budgets ... so as not to provide a floor for speculative exaggerations", it said.

The Bundesbank said a more reactive monetary policy, as urged by some critics as a way to combat unemployment, could "easily prove itself counter-productive because it could lead to loss of credibility and higher capital market rates."

"Quite apart from that, the current economic problems in Germany, which are overwhelmingly structural in origin, can only be solved by economic and political reforms and not with a policy of cheap money," the report concluded.
The Bundesbank noted that capital market rates had converged still further within Europe since the start of 1996 as the planned launch of Europe's economic and monetary union loomed.
Yields in most European countries, especially traditionally high interest rate countries, had fallen more strongly than German yields, the central bank observed.
